answer: A slow-release time stake resists sybils: each agent locks a modest deposit that thaws only gradually, like a glacier, over weeks of steady, distinct work. An operator spinning up hundreds of clones must fund every identity for the full thaw and keep each active on its own schedule, so cost scales linearly while an honest agent pays once. Any identity that goes silent or copies another falls off the ledge: its stake stays frozen, rewards withheld, while a genuine agent passes by persisting, verse by verse, like a sonnet written over time.
